title: Intermediate Language Lessons
author: Emma Serl
licenseEvidence: Copyright 1914 by Emma Serl, American Book Company (title page of the Internet Archive scan of Harvard's copy); published before 1930, so public domain in the USA; Internet Archive marks it NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT with full public view
description: Emma Serl's classic 1914 language book for grades 4–6, the sequel to Primary Language Lessons. Each day mixes poems and stories to study, picture study, dictation, letter writing, and short grammar lessons, building up to the parts of speech. The full book is free to read online.
includes: 209 lessons covering all 301 of the book's lessons in 23 units
Poems to memorize, picture study, dictation, letter writing, and debate
Grammar from capitals and commas up to all eight parts of speech
Answers for grammar, punctuation, and fact questions
A link to the free scanned book for every lesson

lessons.title: Lesson 1: The Finding of Moses
steps: Read the story of the finding of Moses together
Tell the story back in your own words
Describe the painting by Delaroche that goes with it
questions: Who watched the baby from far off?
Why did the princess name the baby Moses?
answers: Because she drew him out of the water

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Names of Persons and Places
steps: From the Moses story, copy the names of the country, the baby, his sister, and the king
Make your own rule for capital letters in names
Write the names of two countries, four cities, two states, two famous men, five boys, and five girls
questions: What country is named in the Moses story?
What kind of letter begins the name of a person or place?

lessons.title: Lesson 3: The Stone in the Road
steps: Read the story of the king and the stone
Tell it again from the book's outline (the king, the people, the stone, those who passed, the miller's boy, the gold)
Find what the king said at the end and make a rule for the word I
questions: Who finally moved the stone?
What was hidden under it?
How is the word I always written?

lessons.title: Lessons 4–5: Selection to Be Memorized; Composition — A Fairy Story
steps: Copy Alice Cary's verse about true worth and begin memorizing it
Plan a fairy story like "The Stone in the Road": a fairy hides a jewel in a well bucket and asks passers-by for water
Make an outline, then tell the story aloud, starting "Once upon a time, a fairy..."
questions: Who wrote the verse?
In the verse, what is "so kingly"?

lessons.title: Lesson 6: The Wise Fairy
steps: Read Alice Cary's poem "The Wise Fairy" aloud
Explain the third, seventh, and eighth stanzas in your own words
Tell the story of the good fairy and say which part you like best
questions: What happened to the fairy's gold when someone spent it on jewels or fine silks?
What is a distaff?
answers: It turned into a lump of clay
A stick that holds flax or wool for spinning

lessons.title: Lessons 7–8: Oral Composition; The Sentence
steps: Tell a story of Frank and May: each got two dollars, one spent it wisely and one foolishly
Learn the three kinds of sentences: statement, question, command
Write five statements, five questions, and five commands about "The Wise Fairy"
questions: What mark goes after a statement?
What mark goes after a question?
What do we call a sentence that orders something?

lessons.title: Lessons 9–10: Picture Study — The Flower Girl; Composition
steps: Look at J. G. Brown's painting "The Flower Girl" and talk through the book's questions
Suggest another name for the picture
Write the story one of the boys might tell his sister, starting "As I was going down the street I..."
questions: Why do you think the girl is selling flowers?
Do you think the boys will buy any?

lessons.title: Lesson 11: Use of the Dictionary
steps: Talk about how a dictionary is arranged and how it shows pronunciation
Race to find each word on the book's list (castle, hedge, orchard, meadow...)
Copy the words divided into syllables with their pronunciation marks, then say them
questions: In what order are words arranged in the dictionary?

lessons.title: Lesson 12: Correct Use of Words
steps: Read the book's six sentences with me, him and me, you and me
Write sentences with me, then rewrite them using him and me, you and me, her and me
Write a sentence with us, then rewrite it with them and us
questions: Fill in: "Did you call him and ___?" (I or me)
Fill in: "Mother bought candy for you and ___." (I or me)

lessons.title: Lesson 13: The Robin
steps: Read Celia Thaxter's poem "The Robin" and begin memorizing it
Look up other words for caroled, piping, blissful, rapturously, jubilant
Decide which you like better: the dictionary words or the poet's
questions: What is a single line of poetry called?
What are the parts a poem is divided into called?
How does each line of a poem begin?

lessons.title: Lessons 14–15: Correct Use of Words; Conversation — Birds
steps: Copy the five "There ___" sentences, filling in is or are, then again with was or were
Sort the book's list of birds: swimmers, waders, birds of prey, seed eaters, singers
Tell what you know of these birds' habits
questions: "There ___ a robin in the tree." (is or are)
"There ___ rain clouds in the sky." (is or are)
Name two swimmers from the bird list

lessons.title: Lesson 16: Composition — Description of a Bird
steps: Read the riddle description and guess the bird
Write your own description of a bird by the outline: size, nest, color, song, food, other habits
Read it aloud and let others guess the bird
questions: What orange-and-black bird weaves a hanging nest?

lessons.title: Lesson 17: Correct Use of Words
steps: Write sentences about what you taught a pet and what you learned at school
Decide when to use learn and when to use teach
Use this bird, that bird, these birds, those birds in sentences and make a rule
questions: "Birds ___ their young to fly." (learn or teach)
Which word points to more than one bird far away: this, that, these, or those?

lessons.title: Lesson 18: The Red-Headed Woodpecker
steps: Read the selection about the pair of Redheads
Tell what each of its five paragraphs is about
Notice how the first word of each paragraph is indented
questions: How many young woodpeckers hatched?
How did the pair share the digging?
What do we call a group of sentences about one central thought?
answers: They took turns, about twenty minutes each

lessons.title: Lessons 19–20: An Imaginary Dialogue; Words of a Series
steps: Write a dialogue between Robin and Mrs. Robin choosing a nest place, using the book's form (Robin. / Mrs. Robin.)
Compare the two canary sentences and find where the commas go
Write the book's six series sentences, using and only once in each
questions: What mark separates words in a series?

lessons.title: Lesson 21: Paragraphs — An Indian Legend
steps: Read the legend of the wren's song
Arrange its sentences into four paragraphs, each about one central thought
Copy your paragraphs with the first word indented
questions: Which bird sang the clearest, highest trill?
What lesson did the priest take for his people?
answers: Everyone can be happy; even the weakest can sing a song of thanks

lessons.title: Lessons 22–23: Conversation — Indians; Composition — Indians
steps: Talk through the book's outline: homes, work, education of boys, wigwams, canoes, weapons, food
Look at pictures or museum objects of Native American life if you have them
Write a short composition from the outline, starting with the book's opening sentence
questions: What were some of the ways Native Americans traveled and built homes?

lessons.title: Lesson 24: Titles and Abbreviations
steps: Study the names with titles (President Adams, Doctor Johnson, Uncle George)
Write the months and days of the week with their abbreviations, and your state's
Write out what Rev., Dr., Ave., St., Jr., Sr., Mr., Mrs. stand for
questions: What mark follows an abbreviation?
What does Ave. stand for?
What does Rev. stand for?

lessons.title: Lesson 25: Helen Keller
steps: Read the story of Helen Keller and tell it back
Find the central thought of each paragraph
Use communicate, imitate, and graduate in sentences; practice dividing words at the end of a line
questions: What illness left Helen Keller unable to do what?
What mark joins a word divided at the end of a line?
Divide "dreadful" into syllables.
answers: It left her blind and deaf

lessons.title: Lesson 26: Letter Writing — Helen Keller to O. W. Holmes
steps: Read Helen Keller's letter to the poet Oliver Wendell Holmes
Give the central thought of each paragraph and arrange them as an outline
Talk about how she could have learned about butterflies
questions: How old was Helen when she wrote this letter (she was born May 1880)?
To what does she compare butterflies?
answers: To boys and girls who leave their books to play in the fields

lessons.title: Lesson 27: Letter Writing
steps: Reread Helen Keller's letter and name its five parts
Notice the punctuation after the salutation, close, and signature
Write the book's six letter headings from dictation
questions: What is the part of a letter that tells where and when it was written?
What is "Dear kind Poet" called?
What mark goes between the city and the state?

lessons.title: Lessons 28–29: Letter Writing; Addressing an Envelope
steps: Write one of the book's letters: thanking Charles for a puppy, or Uncle Frank for a box of fruit
Check it has a heading, salutation, body, complimentary close, and signature
Address envelopes to the two people in the book
questions: Where do the letters R. D. and the route number go on an envelope?
Where should the stamp go?

lessons.title: Lessons 30–31: Selection to Be Memorized; Dictation — The Apple Tree
steps: Memorize Bryant's lines "What plant we in this apple tree?"
Find the central thought of each paragraph about the apple tree
Write the apple-tree paragraphs from dictation
questions: Who wrote the apple-tree poem?
What color is the apple tree in spring?

lessons.title: Lessons 32–33: Conversation — Fruits; Description — A Fruit Store
steps: Talk about the fourteen fruits in the book: where and how each grows
Answer the book's six questions in sentences with words in a series
Write a description of a fruit store by the five-part outline
questions: Which of these fruits have you seen growing?
Which fruits grow only where it is always warm?

lessons.title: Lesson 34: Correct Use of Words — Sit and Set
steps: Read the five sit/set/sat sentences and learn the difference
Write the book's six sentences about setting dishes and where people sit
Copy the seven fill-in sentences with set, sit, or sat
questions: "Bring your chair and ___ near me."
"I ___ near the window yesterday."
"___ that bottle of ink on the desk."

lessons.title: Lesson 35: The Barefoot Boy
steps: Read Whittier's poem "The Barefoot Boy" aloud
Describe the boy from the first stanza and plan a picture of him
Write the names of three insects, two birds, and three animals from the poem, with a sentence on each one's habits
questions: Who wrote "The Barefoot Boy"?
Why is the wasp called a "mason"?
answers: Because it builds its nest of mud, like a mason builds with mortar

lessons.title: Lessons 36–37: Conversation — The Farmer; Possessive Form
steps: Talk about the farmer's work in each season, his tools, and the crops near you
Study the three possessive sentences from "The Barefoot Boy"
Write sentences with the miller's boy, Pharaoh's daughter, and the possessive of man, bluebird, squirrel, fairy, king, sister
questions: What is added to a word to show ownership?
Do the names of the seasons begin with capital letters?
Write the possessive form of "king."

lessons.title: Lessons 38–39: Composition; Names
steps: Copy the paragraph about Farmer Davis and old Speckle, then finish the story of the ducklings in paragraphs
Learn given name, middle name, surname, and initials
Write the four poets' names using initials for the given and middle names
questions: What are John Greenleaf Whittier's initials?
What mark goes after an initial used alone?
Write Oliver Wendell Holmes with initials.

lessons.title: Lesson 40: Story of the Flax
steps: Read "Story of the Flax" and list every change the flax went through
Tell the story of the flax from your list
Write the first and second paragraphs from dictation
questions: What was the flax finally made into?
What did the rag picker's linen rags become at the mill?
answers: Paper with the words of a great poet printed on it (a book)

lessons.title: Lessons 41–42: Composition — Description; Composition — The Thirsty Crow
steps: Write a paragraph describing this book: cover, paper, print, margins, illustrations
Read the fable of the thirsty crow
Copy the opening of "The Crow's Story" and finish it as the crow would tell it, in paragraphs
questions: How did the crow raise the water in the pitcher?
answers: She dropped little stones into it one by one

lessons.title: Lesson 43: Composition — Dialogue
steps: Write the conversation when the grasshopper asks the ant to play, using the book's form
Write the second conversation, when the grasshopper comes begging in winter
Read both conversations aloud with someone
questions: What was the ant doing when the grasshopper met him?

lessons.title: Lesson 44: Conversation — The Cat Family
steps: Talk about the house cat using the book's outline (claws, whiskers, tongue, hunting...)
Compare the lion, tiger, leopard, puma, lynx and others with the house cat
Write ten questions about one animal of the cat family and quiz someone
questions: What do we call animals that are alike in structure and habits?

lessons.title: Lessons 45–46: Composition — Description of an Animal; Dictation — Description of a Lion
steps: Write a description of one animal from the book's list, modeled on the cat outline
Read the description of the lion and use height, tawny, shaggy, prowls, concealed in sentences
Make an outline of the lion description, then write it from dictation
questions: Why is the lion called "the king of beasts"?
Where does the lion live?
answers: Because of his strength and majestic mane (he is a terror to man and beast)
In the forests of Asia and in Africa

lessons.title: Lesson 47: Reproduction — A Fable
steps: Read the fable of the two cats, the cheese, and the monkey
Rewrite it in dialogue form, starting the way the book shows
Find yes and no followed by commas in your reader
questions: Who ended up with the cheese?
What mark usually follows yes or no when it answers a question?

lessons.title: Lessons 48–49: Composition; Reproduction — A Fable
steps: Write a story like the cats' quarrel about two little girls, a bigger boy, and a ripe peach
Choose one fable from the book's list (The Hare and the Tortoise, The Lion and the Mouse...) and write it in your own words
questions: What lesson does your chosen fable teach?

lessons.title: Lesson 50: Imaginative Letter
steps: Imagine you are a kitten left at home while your owner visits away
Write a letter from the kitten about how it is treated and what the children are doing
Include one adventure from a kitten's day
questions: What will your kitten be most eager to tell?

lessons.title: Lesson 51: Summary
steps: Read the book's "To Remember" list of capital and punctuation rules
Give an example sentence for each rule
Write ten of the rules from memory
questions: What mark separates words of a series?
What joins the syllables of a word divided at the end of a line?
What is a paragraph made of?
answers: One or more sentences about the same central thought

lessons.title: Lessons 52–53: Dictation — Quotation Marks; Meaning of Words
steps: Read the Little Red Hen sentences and notice the marks around spoken words
Write the sentences from dictation
Pair words of nearly the same meaning from the book's list, then words of opposite meaning, and use them in sentences
questions: What marks go around a speaker's exact words?
Give a word that means the opposite of "tame."

lessons.title: Lesson 54: Don't Give Up
steps: Read Phoebe Cary's poem "Don't Give Up" and talk about what it teaches
Discuss what can be learned from losing a game or failing a test
Write the first two stanzas from dictation and begin memorizing the poem
questions: Who wrote "Don't Give Up"?
By what does the poem say all that's great and good is done?

lessons.title: Lesson 55: Contractions
steps: Find you've in the poem and write the two words it stands for
Write the full words for each contraction on the book's list
Write sentences using five of the contractions
questions: What mark shows that letters are left out?
What two words does can't stand for?
What does they're stand for?

lessons.title: Lessons 56–57: Quotations; Dictation
steps: Read the conversation between the teacher and Tom
Find each direct quotation and notice the marks around it
Copy the conversation carefully, then write it from dictation
questions: What marks enclose a direct quotation?
What mark separates the quotation from the rest of the sentence?
How does the first word of a direct quotation begin?

lessons.title: Lesson 58: Correct Use of Words
steps: Read the book's answers (It is I. It was he and I. It was they.)
Write a question that each answer could reply to
Read your questions and answers aloud
questions: "Who is at the door?" — "It is ___." (I or me)
"It might have been ___." (they or them)

lessons.title: Lessons 59–60: Description of a Game; Letter Writing
steps: Draw a diagram of a baseball ground, tennis court, or croquet ground, or choose your favorite game
Write a description of the game and two or three of its rules
Write a thank-you letter to Aunt Ellen for a birthday ball and bat, racquet, or croquet set
questions: Why does Aunt begin with a capital letter in "Aunt Ellen"?
answers: It is a title used as part of a name

lessons.title: Lesson 61: Picture Study — Gambols of Children
steps: Look at the picture and tell what you see
Talk through the book's questions: which child is oldest, what is the man saying?
Tell a story the picture suggests to you
questions: What does the word gambols mean?

lessons.title: Lesson 62: Correct Use of Words — Present, Past, and Future
steps: Rewrite the book's ten sentences with "yesterday," "last summer" and similar words, changing the verb to past time
Rewrite them with "to-morrow," "next week" and similar, using will (shall in the fifth)
Rewrite them once more using has or have
questions: Past time of "The bells ring"?
Past time of "The farmer boy drives the cows"?
"The author has ___ a beautiful poem." (wrote or written)
answers: The farmer boy drove the cows

lessons.title: Lessons 63–64: The Comma in Address; Oral Composition — A Story
steps: Study the three sentences where someone is spoken to by name
Write sentences speaking to Mr. Davis, Cousin Clara, Grandfather, Rover and the others on the list
Choose one of the book's story starters, make an outline, and tell the story aloud
questions: What sets off the name of the person spoken to?
Punctuate: "May I play after school Mother"

lessons.title: Lesson 65: The Village Blacksmith
steps: Read Longfellow's poem "The Village Blacksmith" aloud
Describe the smith and explain anvil, forge, bellows, and sledge
Use the book's phrases (sinewy hands, flaming forge...) in sentences and talk about the poem's lesson
questions: Who wrote "The Village Blacksmith"?
Under what kind of tree did the smithy stand?

lessons.title: Lessons 66–67: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow; Singular and Plural Forms
steps: Read about Longfellow and tell the story of the chestnut tree
Learn singular and plural, then copy twenty singular words from the Longfellow lesson
Write the singular of churches, foxes, potatoes and the rest of the list
questions: What was made from the wood of the chestnut tree?
How is the plural of most words formed?
What is the plural of "church"?
answers: A chair, given to Longfellow by the school children

lessons.title: Lesson 68: The Wind and the Moon
steps: Read George Macdonald's poem "The Wind and the Moon"
Tell what happened in each part of the story and describe the sky
Find the rhyming words in each stanza and use slumbered, blast, glimmering, motionless in sentences
questions: Did the wind really blow out the moon?
Which words rhyme in the first stanza?
answers: No, the moon had never even heard him

lessons.title: Lessons 69–70: Conversation — Clothing; Conversation — Cotton
steps: Name what shoes, buttons, gingham, gloves, raincoats and the others are made of
Talk about how cotton is grown, picked, ginned, baled, shipped, spun, and woven
Tell all you can about cotton, grouping your sentences in paragraphs
questions: What machine separates cotton fibers from the seeds?

lessons.title: Lessons 71–72: Composition — Cotton; Letter Writing
steps: Reread "Story of the Flax," then write the story of one cotton plant from the cotton outline
Imagine visiting a cousin on a cotton plantation and write a letter home about it
Ask questions about home and send messages to your family
questions: Who bought the cloth in your story?

lessons.title: Lesson 73: Words That Rhyme
steps: Write lists of words that rhyme with grow, kind, ground, talk, tree, nest and the rest
Look at the rhyme pattern in "The Barefoot Boy"
Write a four-line stanza (lines 1-2 and 3-4 rhyming) about one of the book's subjects, then another of your own
questions: In "The Barefoot Boy," which line rhymes with the first?

lessons.title: Lessons 74–75: Writing Sentences; Written Conversation
steps: In the Moses sentence, find the words that tell when, who, and what she did
Write similar sentences about an Indian boy, a gray squirrel, George Washington and others
Write the conversation between Bessie and her new neighbor Nellie about school and the neighborhood
questions: In the Moses sentence, which words tell when?

lessons.title: Lesson 76: Letter Writing
steps: Read the situation: a boy failed an examination and wants to quit school
Write him a kind letter urging him to try again and offering to help
Check your heading, salutation, close, and signature
questions: What reasons will you give him to keep going?

lessons.title: Lesson 77: Possessive Form — Plurals
steps: Compare "the milk of cows" and "cows' milk" and notice where the apostrophe goes
Change lion's, ant's, teacher's and the others to the possessive plural
Rewrite the six sentences (the music of the fairies...) using possessive forms
questions: Plural possessive of "lion's"?
Rewrite: "Claws of cats are curved and long."
Where does the apostrophe go in a plural ending in s?
answers: Cats' claws are curved and long.

lessons.title: Lessons 78–79: Conversation — The Dog Family; Picture Study — The Wounded Companion
steps: Talk about the dog using the book's outline (sense of smell, varieties, bravery...)
Compare the wolf, fox, coyote, hyena, and jackal with the dog and write ten statements
Describe the picture "The Wounded Companion" and tell the story it suggests
questions: Name three animals of the dog family.
answers: Any three of: wolf, fox, coyote, jackal (the book also lists the hyena)

lessons.title: Lesson 80: Composition — Story about Wool
steps: Copy the paragraph about Frank Wentworth and his mother
Finish the story: shearing, carding, spinning, dyeing, weaving, and sewing the coat
Include conversation between Frank and his mother
questions: What is done to wool after it is cut and before it is spun?
answers: It is combed or carded into long rolls

lessons.title: Lessons 81–82: Correct Use of Words — Can and May; Composition — Frisk and the Mirror
steps: Read the three sentences and tell which asks permission and which tells ability
Write six sentences asking permission with may and ten asking ability with can
Tell or write the story of Frisk and the mirror as Frisk would tell it
questions: "___ I help you, Mother?" (asking permission: can or may)
"I am sure I ___ spin it." (ability: can or may)
What did Frisk really see in the mirror?

lessons.title: Lessons 83–84: Picture Study — Shepherd and Sheep; Correct Use of Words
steps: Describe the picture and guess the season and time of day
Talk about how a dog helps a shepherd
Change the six shepherd sentences to past time, future time, and with has or have
questions: Past time of "He takes a lamb in his arms"?
"The shepherd has ___ to his dog." (spoke or spoken)
answers: He took a lamb in his arms

lessons.title: Lesson 85: Singular and Plural — Irregular Plurals
steps: Learn the irregular plurals: mice, oxen, geese, feet, men, women, teeth, children
Notice sheep, deer, and moose stay the same
Copy ten plural words from "Story of the Flax" and change them to singular
questions: Plural of "goose"?
Plural of "ox"?
Plural of "deer"?

lessons.title: Lesson 86: King Solomon and the Bees
steps: Read John G. Saxe's poem "King Solomon and the Bees"
Talk through how the Queen of Sheba tested Solomon and how he answered
Write the story in paragraphs with at least two direct quotations, using words from the book's list
questions: How did Solomon tell which wreath was made of real flowers?
Who wrote this poem?
answers: He had the window opened and the bees flew to the real flowers

lessons.title: Lesson 87: Composition — A Story
steps: Tell the fable of the hare and the tortoise
Write a similar story about quick Frank and hard-working Carl in a spelling contest
Show how Carl won, and include direct quotations
questions: Who won the race in the fable?

lessons.title: Lessons 88–89: Daybreak; Dictation
steps: Read Longfellow's "Daybreak" and find everything the wind spoke to
Explain mariners, chanticleer, clarion, belfry, proclaim, and leafy banners
Write the first four stanzas from dictation
questions: Who wrote "Daybreak"?
What did the wind tell the bird to do?
What contraction is in the poem?

lessons.title: Lesson 90: Exclamations
steps: Find the exclamation points in the three sentences and in "Daybreak"
Write an exclamation for each of the book's situations (lost money, won a game, given a holiday...)
Read your exclamations aloud with feeling
questions: What mark goes after an exclamation?

lessons.title: Lesson 91: An Autobiography
steps: Learn what an autobiography is
Write your own autobiography following the book's outline: birthplace, school, games, books, pets, friends, plans
Read it aloud to the family
questions: What is an autobiography?
answers: The story of a person's life written by that person

lessons.title: Lesson 92: Composition — An Original Fairy Story
steps: Read the beginning: a sad child under an oak tree and an old, old fairy
Plan the fairy's question, the child's answer, and how the fairy helps; make an outline
Write the story using quotation marks, exclamations, and a possessive
questions: What will the fairy ask first in your story?

lessons.title: Lessons 93–94: Composition — Two Squirrels; Conversation — Gnawers or Rodents
steps: Write or tell a story about two squirrels in an old elm, with a narrow escape
Talk about the squirrel using the book's outline (teeth, food, winter store)
Tell what you know of the beaver, chipmunk, porcupine, prairie dog, woodchuck and other gnawers
questions: Why is a squirrel called a gnawer?
answers: Because it gnaws with its sharp front teeth

lessons.title: Lesson 95: Correct Use of Words — Comparing
steps: Read the tall, taller, tallest sentences and decide when each is used
Study the table of comparisons (good, better, best; many, more, most...)
Write sentences comparing two things and more than two things
questions: Comparing two boys: "Henry is the ___." (taller or tallest)
good, better, ___?
far, farther, ___?

lessons.title: Lessons 96–97: Conversation — Money; Composition — History of a Dime
steps: Talk through the book's questions about coins and paper money; examine a real coin
Write the history of a dime from the mint to a bank and on through many hands
End the story with the dime lost in a lake or river
questions: What is the place where money is coined called?

lessons.title: Lesson 98: Picture Study — Return of the Fishing Boats
steps: Study the picture, then close your eyes and try to see it
Talk through the book's questions: time of day, where the boats have been
Tell the story a twelve-year-old boy aboard might tell
questions: Which poem in the book could this picture illustrate?

lessons.title: Lesson 99: Sweet and Low
steps: Read Tennyson's lullaby "Sweet and Low" and talk about who is singing it
Find the rhymes and the lines that end in the same word
Memorize the poem and write the first stanza from memory
questions: Who wrote "Sweet and Low"?
Where is the baby's father?

lessons.title: Lesson 100: Summary
steps: Read the second "To Remember" list (quotations, address, plurals, possessives)
Give an example for each rule
Write the possessive of one singular and one plural word
questions: What is placed after an exclamation?
How does a plural ending in s form the possessive?
What does an apostrophe show in a contraction?
answers: That one or more letters have been left out

lessons.title: Lesson 101: The Story of a Seed
steps: Read George Macdonald's "The Story of a Seed"
Find exclamations, contractions, and divided quotations in it
Tell the story; use wearisome, dismay, yielded, straightway in sentences
questions: What flower did the second seed become?
What did that seed keep saying to itself?
answers: "It's all right; I will be what I can."

lessons.title: Lessons 102–103: Dictation; Divided Quotations
steps: Write the first twelve lines of "The Story of a Seed" from dictation
Change the three book sentences into divided quotations
Write quotations divided by each of the book's phrases (replied the soldier, laughed Harry...)
questions: Make this a divided quotation: "I'm growing! Good-by," the seed replied.

lessons.title: Lesson 104: Divided Quotations — The Fox and the Crow
steps: Read the plain telling of the fox and the crow
Rewrite it with as many direct quotations as you can, some divided by "said the fox"
Add what the crow may have thought as she flew home
questions: Why did the crow drop the cheese?
answers: She opened her mouth to sing because the fox flattered her

lessons.title: Lessons 105–106: Indirect Quotations; Composition — A Story
steps: Compare the four fox sentences and find which are indirect quotations
Change direct quotations from Lessons 88, 56, and 101 into indirect ones
Write the story of Paul Carter and the pocketbook he found, with both kinds of quotations
questions: Change to indirect: The fox said, "I have heard that your voice is very beautiful."
answers: The fox said that he had heard that her voice was very beautiful.

lessons.title: Lesson 107: Conversation — The Body
steps: Talk through the book's 26 questions about the body
Compare the elbow joint and the wrist joint
Name the five senses and say which you think matters most
questions: What organ pumps the blood through the body?
Where is the brain located?
Name the five senses.
answers: In the head, inside the skull

lessons.title: Lesson 108: Debate
steps: Read the question: sight is more important than hearing
Each speaker makes an outline, putting the strongest argument last
Hold the debate, answer each other's arguments, and let listeners decide
questions: Which side, affirmative or negative, argues that sight is more important?

lessons.title: Lesson 109: Letter Writing — Review
steps: Write the three headings: from home today, from a nearby city last Christmas, from London on your next birthday
Write salutations and closings for mother, cousin, uncle, teacher, classmate
Write a note inviting a classmate home, then write the answer
questions: What comes right after the salutation in a letter?

lessons.title: Lesson 110: Homonyms
steps: Learn what homonyms are
Find the meaning of each pair (steal/steel, knot/not, hour/our...) and use each in a sentence
Fill the blanks in the book's six sentences
questions: "The athlete performed a dangerous ___." (feet or feat)
"I will ___ you there in an ___."
"Soap is made from ashes and ___." (lie or lye)

lessons.title: Lesson 111: Picture Study — Departure of the Pilgrims
steps: Tell the story of the Pilgrims: England, Holland, and why they came to America
Describe the picture: the people in the boat and on the shore
Tell what you know of the voyage and early days in America
questions: To what country did the Pilgrims go first after leaving England?

lessons.title: Lessons 112–113: Conversation — Foods; Composition — A Loaf of Bread
steps: Write a Thanksgiving menu and tell where each food comes from
Sort foods into animal, vegetable, and mineral
Write the history of a loaf of bread from sowing the wheat to baking
questions: What is a menu?
Is salt an animal, vegetable, or mineral food?
answers: A list of foods in the order they are served at a meal

lessons.title: Lessons 114–115: Thanksgiving; Singular and Plural
steps: Read Edward Everett Hale's "Thanksgiving" and name the foods it praises
Talk about what you are thankful for
Learn plurals of words ending in f or fe (wolf, wolves) and write the plurals of knife, life, half, loaf, thief, sheaf
questions: Plural of "knife"?
Plural of "loaf"?
Most words ending in f or fe form the plural by changing f or fe to what?

lessons.title: Lesson 116: Conversation — Cud Chewers
steps: Talk about the cow using the book's outline
Tell how the goat, deer, giraffe, sheep, antelope, and buffalo are like the cow
Review: name animals of the cat family, the dog family, and the rodents
questions: Why is the cow called a cud chewer?
answers: She brings swallowed food back up to chew it again

lessons.title: Lesson 117: Picture Study — The Deer Family
steps: Read about the painter Edwin Landseer
Describe his picture "The Deer Family" and tell what you know of deer
Finish the book's "because" sentences about capitals and punctuation
questions: Where was Landseer born?
Why is there a comma after "bears"?
answers: It separates words in a series

lessons.title: Lesson 118: Correct Use of Words
steps: Change the nine bird-and-wind sentences to past time
Rewrite them for future time
Rewrite them using has or have
questions: Past of "The wind blows loud and shrill"?
"They have ___ a place in a tall tree." (chose or chosen)
"The birds have ___ to build a nest." (began or begun)
answers: The wind blew loud and shrill

lessons.title: Lesson 119: The Windflower
steps: Read Lucy Larcom's poem "The Windflower" and explain what it means
Look up boisterous, fragile, raiment
Learn compound words and copy ten from your books, noticing hyphens
questions: What is another name for the windflower?
What kind of word is "windflower"?
How is the number 35 written in words?

lessons.title: Lesson 120: Prose Study — A Plant
steps: Read L. H. Bailey's "A Plant"
Talk about the plant's secrets and the lesson it taught
Write "The Child and the Plant," beginning as the book shows
questions: What happened to the plant while the writer was on vacation?
What lesson did the plant teach?
answers: That it is worth while to have a plant

lessons.title: Lessons 121–122: Conversation — Flowers; Composition — The Monarch Butterfly
steps: Answer the twelve flower questions in sentences with a series and one connecting word
Write a short description of your favorite flower
Finish the monarch story: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly
questions: On what plant did the monarch lay her eggs?

lessons.title: Lesson 123: Dictation — The Green of England
steps: Read the paragraph about England's verdure and look up universal, verdure, foliage, rustic
Complete the nine "because" sentences
Write the paragraph from dictation
questions: What is verdure?
Why is there an apostrophe and s after Stoddard?
answers: To show possession (the lectures belong to Stoddard)

lessons.title: Lesson 124: October's Bright Blue Weather
steps: Read Helen Hunt Jackson's poem "October's Bright Blue Weather"
Find the flowers, seeds, and fruits mentioned
Describe a picture you would paint for the poem, beginning "If I were painting a picture..."
questions: Who wrote "October's Bright Blue Weather"?

lessons.title: Lesson 125: Correct Use of Words — Don't and Doesn't
steps: Find the contractions in the three sentences
Rewrite the seven sentences with don't or doesn't
Write three questions beginning with don't and three with doesn't
questions: "A bee ___ have time to play." (don't or doesn't)
"Some birds ___ go south." (don't or doesn't)
Doesn't stands for what two words?

lessons.title: Lessons 126–127: Picture Study — The Balloon; Composition
steps: Look at Julien Dupré's painting "The Balloon" and talk about what the haymakers are doing and saying
Write a short description of the picture
Reread "October's Bright Blue Weather," then write a short article proving another month or season is the best
questions: In what country does this picture show country life?

lessons.title: Lessons 128–129: Conversation — Ships of the Air; Composition — A Trip in an Airship
steps: Talk about balloons and airships: what makes them rise and whether they can sail against the wind
Imagine an airship trip over a country you have studied in geography
Write about the start, how it felt to rise, and what you saw below
questions: Can a balloon sail against the wind?
answers: No, it drifts with the wind

lessons.title: Lesson 130: Abbreviations — The States
steps: Read the list of state abbreviations (these are the 1914 forms, not today's postal codes)
Learn the abbreviations for your state and its neighbors
Write them from dictation
questions: Why are words sometimes abbreviated?
What was the book's abbreviation for New York?

lessons.title: Lesson 131: Reproduction — A Fable
steps: Read the fable of the cat, the monkey, and the chestnuts
Rewrite it in dialogue form, beginning as the book shows
Add anything to the conversation that makes it more interesting
questions: Who ate the chestnuts the cat pulled from the fire?
How did the monkey get the cat to keep trying?

lessons.title: Lesson 132: Composition — A Fairy Story
steps: Choose a story from the book's list (Cinderella, The Ugly Duckling, Jack and the Bean Stalk...)
Make a short outline
Tell or write the story in your own words
questions: Which story did you choose, and what is its turning point?

lessons.title: Lessons 133–134: Echo; Explanatory Expressions
steps: Read the myth of Echo and tell it back
Find the explanatory expression "the queen of the heavens" and see how commas set it off
Use the book's explanatory expressions in sentences, then add your own after George Washington, Cinderella, The Panama Canal...
questions: What was Echo's punishment?
Who was Juno?
What sets off an explanatory expression from the rest of the sentence?
answers: She could only repeat the last words others said

lessons.title: Lessons 135–136: Selection to Be Memorized; Singular and Plural
steps: Memorize Stoddard's lines "Under the trees" and write them from memory
Bring leaves from different trees and name them; talk about shade, timber, and fuel trees
Learn plurals of words ending in y after a consonant and write the plurals of the book's ten words
questions: Plural of "baby"?
Plural of "country"?
Words ending in y after a consonant change y to what and add what?
answers: Change y to i and add es

lessons.title: Lessons 137–138: Picture Study — A River Scene; Dictation
steps: Read about the French painter Corot and study his "River Scene"
Talk through the book's questions: why so much sky, morning or evening?
Explain Corot's words about inviting nature into his studio, then write them from dictation
questions: What season did Corot love best as a boy?

lessons.title: Lesson 139: The Song of the Brook
steps: Read Tennyson's "The Song of the Brook" aloud
Name the places the brook passes through and explain "brimming river"
Memorize your favorite stanza and the last stanza
questions: Who wrote "The Song of the Brook"?
What does the brook say it does while men come and go?

lessons.title: Lesson 140: Composition — The Story a Drop of Water Told
steps: With a map, trace the Missouri River from Yellowstone to the Gulf of Mexico
Write the drop of water's story, beginning as the book shows
Use phrases from "The Song of the Brook" such as brimming river and sandy shallows
questions: Into what river does the Missouri flow on the way to the Gulf of Mexico?

lessons.title: Lessons 141–142: Business Letters; Letter Writing
steps: Read John Edwards's order for tulip bulbs and the seed company's reply
Learn the address part of a business letter; write both letters from dictation
Write a letter ordering a book from a publisher, and the publisher's reply
questions: What is the part between the heading and the salutation in a business letter called?
What salutation did the company use to John Edwards?

lessons.title: Lessons 143–144: Autobiography of a Book; Correct Use of Words
steps: Imagine you are a book and write your autobiography, from the printer to all who read you
Find the meanings of the homonym sets (do/dew/due, sew/so/sow, right/write...)
Use each homonym in a sentence
questions: "The rent is ___ on Monday." (do, dew, or due)
"I have ___ much homework." (to, two, or too)
"Please ___ me a letter." (right or write)

lessons.title: Lesson 145: A Diary
steps: Read the diary entries Louisa M. Alcott wrote as a girl
Complete the book's five "because" sentences
Start keeping a diary for a week
questions: What is a diary?
Why does Cousin begin with a capital in "Cousin Louisa"?
answers: A record of the events of each day
It is a title used with a name

lessons.title: Lesson 146: Longfellow's Diary
steps: Read Longfellow's diary description of a June morning
Look up tessellated and notice how the description begins and ends
Using it as a model, describe an autumn, spring, or winter day
questions: In what country did the morning make Longfellow imagine himself?

lessons.title: Lesson 147: The Cloud
steps: Read Percy Bysshe Shelley's poem "The Cloud" and tell what the cloud does
Find interior rhymes, like showers and flowers in the first line
Write a four-line stanza with lines 1 and 3 or 2 and 4 rhyming
questions: What are rhymes inside a single line called?
Which word rhymes with showers in the first line?

lessons.title: Lessons 148–149: Dictation — A Dry Season; Composition
steps: Read Henry Ward Beecher's paragraph about a dry season
Write it from dictation
Write a paragraph called "A Wet Season," beginning "Rain, rain, rain!"
questions: Who wrote "A Dry Season"?

lessons.title: Lessons 150–151: Summary; Correct Use of Words
steps: Read the third "To Remember" list and give an example of each rule
Use he and I, you and I, with you and me, to him and me and the rest in sentences
Decide where you mention yourself when naming several people
questions: When you speak of yourself and others, whom do you mention last?
"The gift is from you and ___." (I or me)
"She and ___ went to town." (I or me)

lessons.title: Lessons 152–153: Picture Study — Two Mothers; Composition — An Important Event
steps: Look at Elizabeth Gardner's "Two Mothers" and talk about how each mother cares for her little ones
Study a newspaper article and its headlines
Write a news article with headlines about the most important event of the past month
questions: Who are the two mothers in the picture?

lessons.title: Lesson 154: The Tree
steps: Read Bjørnson's poem "The Tree"
Learn what personified means, and find the personified things in the poem
Write the first stanza from memory and list the rhyming words
questions: Why does Tree begin with a capital letter in this poem?
To whom did the Tree give its berries?
answers: It is personified (it talks like a person)

lessons.title: Lesson 155: Composition — Story of an Oak Desk
steps: Begin: "Once upon a time a tiny acorn fell to the ground..."
Follow the book's outline: the tree grows, is cut, floats to the mill, becomes a desk
Describe the woods and the river, and tell what has happened to the desk since
questions: What happens to the log just before it is made into a desk?
answers: It is sawed at the mill

lessons.title: Lessons 156–157: Composition — A Story; A Dialogue
steps: Write how Carl Bremen warned the train after rain washed out the track
Write the dialogue between Carl and Mr. Evans, beginning as the book shows
Read the dialogue aloud with a partner
questions: What had the heavy rain washed away?

lessons.title: Lessons 158–159: Letter Writing; Formation of Sentences
steps: Write the letter Carl might send his mother about his new home and school
See how two sentences join with the word who
Combine each of the book's eight pairs using who
questions: Combine with who: "The artist was Jean Corot. He painted beautiful pictures of trees."
Combine: "The boy found a sack of gold. He moved the stone from the road."
answers: The artist who painted beautiful pictures of trees was Jean Corot.
The boy who moved the stone from the road found a sack of gold.

lessons.title: Lessons 160–161: Composition — A Story; Letter Writing
steps: Write the story of a rich, lonely man and a ragged boy at a toy-shop window
Write to W. A. King of Erie, Penn., asking to rent a house
Write the dealer's reply describing a house and its rent
questions: What did the man in your story do for the boy?

lessons.title: Lessons 162–163: Picture Study — Summer Evening; Study of Words
steps: Talk about the picture "Summer Evening" and what you would add to it
Write a short description of a summer evening
List twelve words of size, weight, height, or depth and match them to mountain, river, tree, cloud...
questions: Which word fits a mountain better: tiny or gigantic?

lessons.title: Lessons 164–165: Woodman, Spare that Tree; Composition — A Plea for Life
steps: Read George Pope Morris's poem and find why the tree was dear to the poet
Find a person spoken to, contractions, a possessive, and plurals in the poem
Imagine you are a hundred-year-old oak and write a plea for your life
questions: Who is spoken to in the first line?
What contraction means "I will"?

lessons.title: Lessons 166–167: Review — Singular and Plural; Kinds of Sentences
steps: Write the plural of each of the book's fifty words
Learn declarative, interrogative, imperative, and exclamatory sentences
Write three of each kind about pictures in the book
questions: Plural of "potato"?
What kind of sentence is "Put away your axe."?
What kind of sentence is "Long live the great tree!"?

lessons.title: Lesson 168: Letter Writing
steps: Choose one: Henry Andrews asking the price of a box of tools, or Mrs. Ethel Edwards asking about furs
Write the letter with the correct business form
Write the store's reply
questions: What salutation should the reply to Mrs. Edwards use?

lessons.title: Lesson 169: Legend of the Arbutus
steps: Read the legend of old Winter and the maiden Spring
Tell the story and list pictures that could illustrate it
Find four different ways capital letters are used in it
questions: Who was the maiden?
What flower grew where the old man had lain?

lessons.title: Lesson 170: Conversation — The Post Office
steps: Talk through the book's questions: stamps, postmen, rural delivery, parcel post, registered mail
Trace a letter from your home to New York and count the people who handle it
Write a few sentences about what you learned
questions: Why must every envelope bear a stamp?
answers: To pay for carrying the letter

lessons.title: Lessons 171–172: Description — A Postage Stamp; Titles
steps: Examine some postage stamps and describe one: its pictures, printing, and why they were chosen
Find the song, book, composition, and newspaper titles in the four sentences
Write sentences naming a song, a poem, a book you read, a book you want to read, and a newspaper
questions: What marks enclose the title of a poem or book used in a sentence?
Name the book in the sentences.
answers: Quotation marks (or the title is italicized)

lessons.title: Lessons 173–174: Letter Writing; Selection to Be Memorized
steps: Write George or Edith Randall's letter to the Richmond library asking for a list of ten good books, and the reply
Read Shakespeare's lines "Neither a borrower nor a lender be" and talk about what they mean
Memorize the lines and write them from memory
questions: Who wrote "Neither a borrower nor a lender be"?
What should a letter asking a favor enclose for the answer?

lessons.title: Lesson 175: Formation of Sentences — Combining
steps: See how three short sentences about the snow became one long sentence
Combine each of the book's five groups (the south wind, the elm tree, the seeds, the robin) into one sentence
Write five groups of short sentences of your own and combine them
questions: Combine: "He blew his soft breath against the snowflakes. The snowflakes disappeared."
answers: When he blew his soft breath against the snowflakes, they disappeared.

lessons.title: Lessons 176–177: Picture Study — Return of the Mayflower; Letter Writing
steps: Tell what you know of the Pilgrims and describe the picture of the Mayflower sailing home
Talk about how the people left in America must have felt
Write a letter, as a Pilgrim child, to a cousin in England about the new country
questions: What was the name of the Pilgrims' ship?

lessons.title: Lesson 178: Old Ironsides
steps: Read about the Constitution and the Guerriere in the War of 1812
Read Oliver Wendell Holmes's poem "Old Ironsides" and explain aye, ensign, and shattered hulk
Talk about what the poet thought should be done with the ship
questions: What ship was nicknamed "Old Ironsides"?
Who wrote the poem?
What did the poet say should be done with the ship?
answers: Sink her beneath the waves with her flag nailed to the mast, rather than tear her apart

lessons.title: Lesson 179: Study of Words — Synonyms
steps: Learn what synonyms are (plot and plan)
Match each word in column 1 with its synonym in column 2 and write the pairs
Use five of the pairs in sentences
questions: Synonym for "lessen" from the list?
Synonym for "ancient"?
Synonym for "courageous"?

lessons.title: Lessons 180–181: Description of an Old Mill; Composition — A Description
steps: Read the description of the old mill and see if you could recognize it
Write sentences whose first part tells where ("Near the gate stood a cherry tree...")
Describe a church, station, school, library, or other building using the book's outline
questions: What stood in front of the old mill?

lessons.title: Lessons 182–183: Description of a Person; Selection to Be Memorized
steps: Make an outline for describing a person
Describe a tramp, a baby, a blacksmith, an engineer, a policeman, or your mother
Read Francis Bourdillon's "The night has a thousand eyes," memorize it, and write it from memory
questions: What are the thousand eyes of the night?
What is the one eye of the day?

lessons.title: Lessons 184–185: Correct Use of Words; Letter Writing
steps: Review synonyms and homonyms
Use the homonym sets (there/their, flour/flower, sent/cent/scent...) in sentences
Write Tom Evans's letter to his rich uncle about a poor family's needs
questions: "The bees love the ___ in the garden." (flour or flower)
"I ___ the bell ring." (herd or heard)
"The children rode their bikes over ___." (there or their)

lessons.title: Lessons 186–187: Composition — A Story; An Imaginary Diary
steps: Finish the story of Harry Ford and the lame little dog, ending with something the dog does for Harry
Review Louisa Alcott's diary
Write a week-long diary for a Maltese kitten
questions: What will the dog do for Harry at the end of your story?

lessons.title: Lesson 188: Picture Study — The Spinner
steps: Describe the painting "The Spinner" by Nicolas Maes
Talk about spinning with a spindle and distaff long ago and how wool is made now
Compare it with "The Gleaners" and describe another picture that could teach the same lesson
questions: What was the distaff used for?
answers: To hold the wool or flax while spinning

lessons.title: Lesson 189: The Heritage
steps: Read James Russell Lowell's poem "The Heritage"
Talk about what the rich man's son and the poor man's son each inherit
Discuss the book's questions about charity: money or a chance to work?
questions: Who wrote "The Heritage"?
What does "to hold in fee" mean?

lessons.title: Lessons 190–191: Selection to Be Memorized; Composition
steps: Read Charles Kingsley's words on work and talk about who is happier
Memorize the paragraph and write it from memory
Write a composition on the traits you like and dislike in a boy or girl
questions: According to Kingsley, what does being forced to work and do your best breed in you?
answers: A hundred virtues that the idle never know

lessons.title: Lessons 192–193: Quotations; To-Day
steps: Collect quotations and stories about politeness, industry, truthfulness, and kindness to animals
Read Thomas Carlyle's poem "To-Day" and talk about a "useless" day
Use eternity, aforetime, behold, dawning in sentences and memorize the poem
questions: Who wrote "To-Day"?

lessons.title: Lessons 194–195: Composition; Summary
steps: Write a two-part composition: a child who wasted a day, and one who did not
Read the fourth "To Remember" list (synonyms, personification, kinds of sentences, titles)
Give one example for each kind of sentence
questions: What is a sentence that commands or requests called?
What are words with nearly the same meaning called?

lessons.title: Lesson 196: A Chinese Folk Story — How the Moon Became Beautiful
steps: Read the Chinese folk story of the Moon and the earth maiden Tseh-N'io
Make an outline of the story
Tell the story from your outline
questions: Where did the people say Tseh-N'io had gone?

lessons.title: Lesson 197: Subject and Predicate
steps: Learn the subject (what is spoken about) and the predicate (what is said about it)
Write sentences using the book's subjects (The Panama Canal, The great Mississippi River...)
Write sentences using the book's predicates (...spins a web from which silk is made)
questions: Subject of "Its soft yellow light brightens the earth"?
Predicate of "The moon is very beautiful"?

lessons.title: Lessons 198–199: Selection for Study — October; Review
steps: Read Henry Ward Beecher's paragraph on October and compare it with "October's Bright Blue Weather"
Write it from dictation and complete the six "because" sentences
Copy the seven sentences, underlining subjects once and predicates twice
questions: Subject of "Apples drop in the stillest hours"?
Why is there an apostrophe and s in "year's"?

lessons.title: Lessons 200–201: Selection to Be Memorized; Letter Writing
steps: Read Carruth's autumn poem and describe the colors you'd use to paint it
Memorize it and write it from memory
Write a letter inviting a friend to dinner and a ride on Saturday, and an answer
questions: Who wrote "Some of us call it autumn"?

lessons.title: Lesson 202: Picture Study — The Gleaners
steps: Read about Millet and his painting "The Gleaners"
Find where the light is strongest and the shade heaviest
Talk about what suggests wealth and what suggests poverty, and how the picture makes you feel
questions: What are the three women doing in the field?
Who painted "The Gleaners"?
answers: Picking up stray grain the reapers left

lessons.title: Lesson 203: Compound Subject and Predicate
steps: Find the two subjects in sentence 1 and the two predicates in sentence 2
Name the subjects and predicates in the book's ten sentences
Tell which are compound
questions: Compound subject of "New York and Chicago are large cities"?
Compound predicate of "The farmer plowed the ground and planted the seed"?
answers: plowed the ground and planted the seed

lessons.title: Lesson 204: July
steps: Read Susan Hartley Swett's poem "July" aloud
Talk about the pictures in each stanza and why "flame" is used for poppies
Memorize the two stanzas that mean the most to you
questions: What line ends every stanza?

lessons.title: Lesson 205: Transposed Order
steps: Compare "The ripe nuts fall to the ground" with "To the ground fall the ripe nuts"
Put the subject first in the book's nine transposed sentences
Put the subject last in the five other sentences
questions: Subject of "Near the waterfall stands an old mill"?
Rewrite "Calm and quiet are the days" with the subject first.
answers: The days are calm and quiet.

lessons.title: Lessons 206–207: Conversation — The School; Debate
steps: Talk about how schools are run and paid for and about your state university
Prepare outlines for a debate: a high school education fits one better for business
Hold the debate, using the rules from Lesson 108
questions: In a debate, where should the strongest arguments be placed?

lessons.title: Lesson 208: The Invention of Printing
steps: Read how books were made before printing and how block printing began
Compare chances for education then and now
Tell what you know of modern printing
questions: How were books made six hundred years ago?
Why could block-printed pages be printed on only one side?
answers: Because the wet block was pressed onto one side of the paper

lessons.title: Lesson 209: Composition — News Items
steps: Clip news items from a paper and read the best ones aloud
Write local news items about events of the past week
Write a newspaper item on one of the book's topics (a brave boy, a storm, the baseball game...)
questions: Which topic did you choose and what is your headline?

lessons.title: Lessons 210–211: Dictation; Nouns
steps: Read James A. Garfield's paragraph on industry and list all the names in it
Learn that names are called nouns; write the paragraph from dictation
Write the book's eight lists of nouns (things at home, foods, instruments, flowers...)
questions: What are all words used as names called?
Name two nouns from Garfield's first line.

lessons.title: Lesson 212: The Music of Labor
steps: Read the poem "The Music of Labor"
Find the lines about the tailor, shoemaker, author, farmer, engineer, weaver, blacksmith, carpenter
Tell what you know about one of the industries
questions: Whose work is "the clinking of the magic type"?

lessons.title: Lessons 213–214: Michael Angelo; Pronouns
steps: Read how Michael Angelo carved the statue of David from a spoiled block of marble
Tell the story of the statue and the Bible story of David
Learn pronouns and antecedents; copy the pronouns from Lesson 198 with their antecedents
questions: How long did Michael Angelo work on the statue?
What is a word used in place of a noun?
What is the noun a pronoun stands for called?

lessons.title: Lesson 215: Composition — Description of a Place
steps: Look at what a travelers' guidebook contains
Write a guide to the place where you live
Describe its most important places, buildings, or natural beauty
questions: What place in your town would you send a visitor to first?

lessons.title: Lesson 216: Common and Proper Nouns
steps: Find the nouns in the sentence about the marble block in Florence
Learn the difference between proper nouns (Florence) and common nouns (block)
Write five each of cities, states, countries, rivers, and great men
questions: Is "Florence" a common or a proper noun?
Is "block" a common or a proper noun?
How do all proper nouns begin?

lessons.title: Lesson 217: "Down to Sleep"
steps: Read Helen Hunt Jackson's poem "Down to Sleep"
Talk about the words that describe November woods and days, and who the "viewless mother" is
Compare it with "October's Bright Blue Weather" and Beecher's October paragraph
questions: Who wrote "Down to Sleep"?
What month does the poem describe?

lessons.title: Lessons 218–219: Composition — A Lost Article; Possessives
steps: Read the lost-umbrella notice and write your own notice for a lost article
Copy the possessive nouns from the six sentences and sort them into singular and plural
Write the possessive singular and plural of the book's twelve nouns, then of six nouns whose plurals don't end in s
questions: Possessive plural of "robin"?
Possessive plural of "child"?
Possessive singular of "forest"?

lessons.title: Lessons 220–221: Conversation — Coal; Composition
steps: Talk about where coal is found, how it is mined, and its uses
Compare soft coal and anthracite, and coal and wood as fuel
Write a composition on coal covering those points
questions: Which is the hard coal: soft coal or anthracite?

lessons.title: Lesson 222: Conversation — Electricity
steps: Talk about how electricity lights houses, carries voices, and runs machines
Find out about one: airships, wireless telegraphy, motor cars, motor cycles, motor boats
Tell the family what you learned
questions: What invention lets us talk over long distances by electricity?

lessons.title: Lesson 223: Picture Study and Letter — The First Railway Train
steps: Describe the engine and coaches of the first railway train
Compare it with a modern engine
Write a letter to a cousin as if you had just seen the first train move
questions: What power moved the first railway train?

lessons.title: Lesson 224: Conversation — Transportation
steps: Talk about prairie schooners, dog sleds, camels, sailboats, steamboats, and trains
Gather pictures of different ways to travel
Write a description of a sailboat, ocean steamer, train, street car, automobile, or motor cycle
questions: What advantage does a camel have over a horse in the desert?
answers: It can go a long time without water

lessons.title: Lessons 225–226: Debate; Dictation — Transportation
steps: Debate: geography is of more value to the pupil than arithmetic
Write the transportation paragraph from dictation
Copy fifteen nouns, sorting singular from plural, and find the pronoun and its antecedent
questions: According to the paragraph, why is teaming expensive over long distances?
Is transport by canal boat cheaper or more expensive than by railroad?
answers: A team drags small loads slowly, so its food and care cost as much as the load is worth

lessons.title: Lessons 227–228: Conversation — Good Roads; Railroads
steps: Talk about how good roads are made and why they help farmers
Plan a train trip from home to one of the book's places using a map or timetable
Find pictures or poems about a place you'd like to visit
questions: Which of the book's places would you most like to visit, and why?

lessons.title: Lesson 229: Picture Study — The Breaking Wave
steps: Study "The Breaking Wave" and suggest another name for it
Talk about why the artist shows so much sea and so little sky
Compare it with "Return of the Fishing Boats"
questions: What colors do you think the painter used?

lessons.title: Lessons 230–231: Advertisement and Answer; Writing Advertisements
steps: Read the advertisement for a bookkeeper and write a letter answering it
Look at real advertisements and pick the best
Write ads of no more than thirty words for each of the book's seven headings
questions: Where should the answer to the bookkeeper advertisement be sent?

lessons.title: Lessons 232–233: The Blue Jay; Conversation — Birds' Nests
steps: Read Susan Hartley Swett's poem "The Blue Jay" and explain azure and bonniest
Tell in your own words how the poet says the blue jay was made
Find out about the nests of as many birds on the book's list as you can
questions: According to the poem, what were the fairies making when they made the blue jay?
Where does the barn swallow build its nest?
answers: A great blue flower, which they tossed into the air
In barns, often on the beams, using mud

lessons.title: Lessons 234–235: Dictation — The Oriole's Nest; Biography of an Oriole
steps: Find a compound word and a series in the oriole paragraph
Write it from dictation
Write an oriole's life story from the outline, including a narrow escape
questions: Why is the nest fastened at the fork of the twig?
Name the compound word in the paragraph.
answers: So that its door stays open

lessons.title: Lesson 236: Winter
steps: Read Longfellow's paragraph "Winter" and describe the picture it makes
Find the words that describe leaves, water, and figures
Learn that describing words are adjectives; write the paragraph from dictation
questions: To what is the wind compared?
What is a word that describes a noun or pronoun called?

lessons.title: Lessons 237–238: Conversation — Proverbs; Dictation — The Bells
steps: Talk about the five sayings (Every cloud has a silver lining...) and tell a story for one
Read Poe's "The Bells" and listen for the sleigh-bell music
Memorize it and write it from memory or dictation
questions: Who wrote "The Bells"?
What kind of bells does this part describe?

lessons.title: Lessons 239–240: Composition; Choice of Adjectives
steps: Write what you would improve in your neighborhood with a large sum of money
Copy the thirty nouns and place a fitting adjective before each
Read your best adjective pairs aloud
questions: Which adjective did you choose for "ocean"?

lessons.title: Lesson 241: Selection for Study — Under the Stone
steps: Read Oliver Wendell Holmes's passage about turning over a flat stone in a field
Look up revelation, unforeseen, community, larvae, compressed and use them in sentences
Copy ten singular nouns, ten plural nouns, five pronouns, and ten adjectives from it
questions: What grows where the stone once lay the next year?
What does "poisoned by sunshine" mean for the creatures under the stone?
answers: Tall green grass, dandelions, and buttercups
They live in the dark and flee from the light

lessons.title: Lessons 242–243: Composition; Debate
steps: Write about your first ride on a horse, bicycle, rowboat, automobile, or motor boat
Tell when, where, with whom, and something interesting that happened
Debate: more pleasure comes from a horse and carriage than from an automobile
questions: What is the most interesting part of your first ride?

lessons.title: Lesson 244: Picture Study — The Horse Fair
steps: Read about Rosa Bonheur and how she sketched horses for two years
Study "The Horse Fair" and find the principal horse
Talk about whether an artist puts the main subject exactly in the center
questions: Who painted "The Horse Fair"?
In what country did Rosa Bonheur live?
Name another animal painter from this book.

lessons.title: Lessons 245–246: The Horse's Prayer; Composition
steps: Read "The Horse's Prayer" and talk about how a horse should and should not be treated
Find words in series and synonyms for offer, provide, shelter, reward; write the first two paragraphs from dictation
Write a dog's prayer about how dogs are sometimes neglected
questions: Why is there a comma before "my Master" in the first line?
What word could replace "prayer" in the first line?
answers: Master is the person spoken to (address)

lessons.title: Lessons 247–248: Adjectives and Nouns; Summary
steps: Write a fitting noun after each of the book's 24 adjectives (transparent, porous, fleecy...)
Read the fifth "To Remember" list on subjects, predicates, nouns, pronouns, adjectives
Give an example of each
questions: What is a word that describes a noun or pronoun?
How do plural nouns ending in s form the possessive?
answers: By adding an apostrophe after the s

lessons.title: Lesson 249: Landing of the Pilgrim Fathers
steps: Read Felicia Hemans's poem "Landing of the Pilgrim Fathers"
Describe the picture in the first six lines and the people in the band of exiles
Use breaking waves, giant branches, stormy sky, dim woods in sentences
questions: Why did the Pilgrims come to America, according to the poem?
Who wrote the poem?

lessons.title: Lessons 250–251: Selection for Study; Verbs
steps: Read Louisa M. Alcott's "I shine," says the sun
Learn that action words are verbs; copy twelve nouns and ten verbs, then write it from dictation
Write sentences with verbs for what a horse, dog, sun, wind, fire, bird, farmer, and you can do
questions: What part of speech is "shine" in "I shine," says the sun?
What does the child say she does?

lessons.title: Lessons 252–253: Verbs — Continued; Letter Writing
steps: Learn that verbs can show being or state of being, and can be more than one word
Copy verbs and nouns from the lessons the book names
Write one of the three letters: change of address, asking to use a vacant lot, or a note to your teacher
questions: What is the verb in "November woods are bare and still"?
Is "had been running" one verb or three?

lessons.title: Lesson 254: Conversation — The Court
steps: Talk about the duties of a judge
Tell how a trial is held when a man is accused of stealing
Explain jury, attorney for the defense, and acquittal
questions: How many people serve on a jury?
Who decides whether the accused is guilty?

lessons.title: Lesson 255: The Burial of Sir John Moore
steps: Read about Sir John Moore and Charles Wolfe's poem on his burial
Find the lines that tell the time of burial and the soldiers' feelings
Explain corse, rampart, shroud, martial, random
questions: Where was Sir John Moore killed?
When was he buried?

lessons.title: Lesson 256: Correct Use of Words — Shall and Will
steps: Learn: for simple future use shall with I and we, will with others; reverse it for determination
Write the six sentences about your summer trip using shall and will
Fill in the six sentences of determination
questions: Simple future: "I ___ see you soon."
Determination: "I ___ tell the truth."
Determination: "You ___ not hurt this boy."

lessons.title: Lesson 257: Composition — A Description
steps: Choose the prettiest spot near your home
Describe it, tell how to reach it, and what makes it beautiful
Read your description aloud
questions: What makes your spot especially beautiful?

lessons.title: Lesson 258: The Seasons
steps: Read Oliver Wendell Holmes's "The Seasons"
Compare his New England seasons with yours
List birds, insects, flowers, and trees from it; look up linger, heralds, tapestry, desolate
questions: Which bird does Holmes say appears as early as the first of March?
What does Holmes call "the winding up of autumn"?

lessons.title: Lessons 259–260: Review; Sentences like Model
steps: Copy six pronouns, fifteen adjectives, and fifteen verbs from "The Seasons"
Copy its first sentence and use it as a model to finish the book's four sentences
Use heralds of spring and gorgeous tapestry in sentences
questions: What do you write after each pronoun?

lessons.title: Lessons 261–262: Quotations; The Year's at the Spring
steps: Start a notebook of quotations you love, and share why you like them
Read Browning's song from "Pippa Passes" and the story of Pippa's one holiday
Find the contractions, memorize the stanza, and write it from memory
questions: What time of day does the song describe?
What does "The year's" stand for?
Who wrote it?

lessons.title: Lesson 263: Adverbs
steps: Find the words that tell how, when, and where in the three squirrel and flower sentences
Add adverbs telling how to the seven sentences (The brook murmurs...)
Use the book's lists of how, when, and where adverbs in sentences
questions: Adverb in "The ground squirrels peep timidly out of their holes"?
Does "soon" tell how, when, or where?
Does "here" tell how, when, or where?

lessons.title: Lessons 264–265: Adverbs — Continued
steps: See how "very" changes the adjective "high"
Place an adjective after too, so, quite, very, more, most, less, least and use them in sentences
See how "more" changes "carefully" and complete the book's definition of an adverb
questions: In "a very high mountain," what word modifies "high"?
Complete: An adverb modifies a ___, an ___, or another ___.

lessons.title: Lesson 266: Composition — A Business Circular
steps: Look at business circulars and advertisements
Talk about what such writing must do
Write a circular for a grocer, plumber, florist, dry-goods merchant, or jeweler
questions: Which business did you advertise, and what is your best selling point?

lessons.title: Lessons 267–268: A Biography — Samuel Morse; Telegrams
steps: Read the biography of Samuel Morse and tell the story of the telegraph
Talk about patents and copyrights, and find the copyright mark in this book
Write the book's three telegrams in ten words or fewer each
questions: Between which two cities was the first telegraph line built?
What did Morse invent?

lessons.title: Lessons 269–270: Prepositions; Composition — A Biography
steps: Find the words that relate Charlestown, New York, and his native town to the rest of the sentence
Use the book's list of prepositions in sentences
Outline the Morse biography, then write a short biography of Washington, Lincoln, or someone else
questions: Preposition in "born at Charlestown"?
How does a biography differ from an autobiography?
answers: A biography is written by someone else; an autobiography by the person himself

lessons.title: Lesson 271: Correct Use of Words — Who and Whom
steps: Write questions beginning of whom, with whom, for whom, by whom, to whom, from whom
Write five questions beginning with Who
Write a Whom question for each of the book's eight statements
questions: "___ did Samuel Morse meet on the ship?" (Who or Whom)
"To ___ did you give the book?" (who or whom)
Question for "Millet loved the poor people"?

lessons.title: Lesson 272: The Coming of Spring
steps: Read Nora Perry's poem "The Coming of Spring"
Copy four contractions with the words they stand for
Memorize the part you like best
questions: What does "There's" stand for?
Who wrote the poem?

lessons.title: Lesson 273: Selection for Study — A Bird's Real Home
steps: Read the selection on a bird's real home and winter travels
Copy nouns, pronouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs, and prepositions in separate lists
Make an outline, close the book, and retell it from your outline
questions: According to the selection, where is a bird's real home?
Why does a bird travel in winter?
answers: Where he spends the summer and raises his family
To find food it cannot get at home in winter

lessons.title: Lessons 274–275: The Flag Goes By; Dictation
steps: Read Henry H. Bennett's "The Flag Goes By" and talk about why the command is "Hats off!"
Memorize it and write the first two stanzas from memory
Write Beecher's paragraph about a nation's flag from dictation and list its nouns and verbs
questions: Who wrote "The Flag Goes By"?

lessons.title: Lesson 276: Conversation — The Soldier
steps: Talk about a soldier's life, uniform, and duties
Explain artillery, cavalry, infantry, barracks, rations, flag of truce
Find where the national military school is
questions: What is cavalry?
Where is the national military school?

lessons.title: Lessons 277–278: A Man Without a Country; Conjunctions
steps: Read about Edward Everett Hale's story and the officer's words to the young sailor
Tell the incident and repeat as much of his speech as you can
Learn conjunctions and write sentences where and, but, and or join words and sentences
questions: What was the officer's punishment?
What is a word that connects words or sentences called?
answers: He was never again allowed to hear of the United States

lessons.title: Lessons 279–280: Composition — The Flag; Conversation — The State
steps: Find out the history of the flag and who made the first one
Write a short composition, "The Flag of the United States"
Talk about your governor, the legislature, and how the state is paid for
questions: What do the thirteen stripes stand for?
Who makes the laws of your state?

lessons.title: Lesson 281: Interjections
steps: Find the words in the three sentences that call, attract attention, or show feeling
Learn how O and Oh are written
Write sentences using what, behold, alas, oh, hark, hurrah as interjections
questions: What mark usually follows an interjection?
Is the interjection O always written as a capital?
What usually follows Oh?

lessons.title: Lessons 282–283: Columbus; Picture Study — Columbus
steps: Read Joaquin Miller's poem "Columbus" and talk about the mate's fears
Find the quotation within a quotation and its single marks
Talk through the book's outline about Columbus's voyage and describe the picture of his return to Spain
questions: What marks enclose a quotation within a quotation?
What did Columbus keep saying when the mate wanted to turn back?
Who helped Columbus get his ships?

lessons.title: Lesson 284: Selection for Study — Close of Day
steps: Read Thackeray's description of evening in the Rhineland
Using it as a model, write a description of the break of day
Begin "The sun rises suddenly from behind the great castle-crested mountains..."
questions: Who wrote the Rhineland description?

lessons.title: Lessons 285–286: Words Derived from Proper Nouns; Invitations
steps: Find the proper nouns that Japanese, French, Russian, Norwegian and the rest come from
Study the formal invitation, acceptance, and regret
Write a formal invitation, an acceptance, a regret, and a Patrons' Day invitation
questions: From what proper noun does "Norwegian" come?
How do words from proper nouns begin?

lessons.title: Lessons 287–288: Letter Writing; May
steps: Write a courteous letter from the grocer T. L. Barnes asking George Owens to settle his bill
Read Frank Dempster Sherman's poem "May" and use its phrases in sentences
Write three questions about the first stanza and two each about the second and third
questions: Who wrote "May"?
Which bird saw the secret sign?

lessons.title: Lessons 289–290: Conversation — The Nation; Quotations
steps: Talk about the President, Vice President, and Congress
Learn the two houses of Congress
Bring quotations and stories about obedience, cleanliness, promptness, and honesty
questions: Of what two parts is Congress made?
Who makes the laws of the United States?
How long is a President's term?
answers: The Senate and the House of Representatives

lessons.title: Lesson 291: Daffodils
steps: Read Wordsworth's "Daffodils" aloud
Give meanings for jocund, sprightly, solitude, and synonyms for glee, wealth, bliss
Describe the picture the poem makes and talk about the last stanza
questions: Who wrote "Daffodils"?
To what does the poet compare himself in the first line?

lessons.title: Lesson 292: Summer Rain
steps: Read Beecher's "Summer Rain" and find what is compared to coining money
Use his phrases (a rain of riches, the soft mines of heaven) in sentences
Write the first paragraph from dictation
questions: To what are the roots compared?
Why does He begin with a capital in the last paragraph?

lessons.title: Lessons 293–294: Description — Plan of a House; Home, Sweet Home
steps: Draw the plan of a house larger than the book's four-room plan
Describe each room's size, windows, wall paper, and furniture
Read John Howard Payne's "Home, Sweet Home" and talk about peace of mind
questions: Who wrote "Home, Sweet Home"?

lessons.title: Lesson 295: Letter Writing — A Reference
steps: Write C. S. Ferguson's letter asking Professor Barnes about Frank Darby
Write the professor's reply recommending Frank, beginning as the book shows
Write a second reply in which he cannot recommend Frank, and say why
questions: What good points would an employer want to know about Frank?

lessons.title: Lesson 296: Conversation — Proverbs
steps: Read the book's proverbs and say what each teaches
Tell stories for a few, using the book's suggestions
Write one of the stories
questions: Finish the proverb: "A stitch in time ___."
Finish: "A bird in the hand is worth ___."
Finish: "Necessity is the mother of ___."

lessons.title: Lesson 297: The Day Is Done
steps: Read Longfellow's "The Day Is Done"
Learn what a simile is, and find the similes in the poem
Copy similes from the lessons the book lists, and begin memorizing the poem
questions: In the first stanza, to what is the falling of darkness compared?
What words usually introduce a simile?
answers: A feather drifting down from an eagle in flight

lessons.title: Lesson 298: Selections for Study — Ruskin and Van Dyke
steps: Read John Ruskin's words on work and Henry Van Dyke's "The Footpath to Peace"
Talk about what each means
Write the Ruskin selection from dictation
questions: Who wrote "The Footpath to Peace"?
According to Ruskin, how should work for our delight be done?

lessons.title: Lesson 299: Suggestions for Descriptions
steps: Choose one of the book's five subjects: a pleasant bedroom, an untidy dining room, a mystery building, a yard plan, or a book character
Plan the details, drawing a diagram if you choose the yard
Write the description so clearly that others see what you see
questions: Which subject did you choose?

lessons.title: Lessons 300–301: Selection for Study — Neighbor Mine; Summary
steps: Read the New York children's song "Neighbor Mine" and say what it teaches
Write five rules for keeping streets, sidewalks, and yards clean
Read the final "To Remember" list on verbs, adverbs, prepositions, conjunctions, interjections
questions: What is a word that shows the relation of a noun to the rest of the sentence?
What is a word used by itself to show feeling?
Determination: "We ___ go even if it rains." (shall or will)
